claims.text: A hierarchical machine-learning model can use measured microstructural descriptors to predict Young’s modulus, yield strength, and fracture behavior of HfNbTiVAl10.
The proposed model can predict these properties more accurately than full-field atomistic or continuum simulations.
The proposed model can predict these properties at lower computational cost than full-field atomistic or continuum simulations.
The HfNbTiVAl10 initial state has a primary disordered BCC matrix containing nanoscale secondary phases and refined grain boundaries.
Grain-size distributions, secondary-phase volume fraction and size, and phase-boundary connectivity are suitable structural inputs for the predictive model.
Secondary-phase morphology and its distribution between the matrix and grain boundaries are associated with mechanical-property changes in refractory high-entropy alloys.
The listed microstructural descriptors govern dislocation nucleation and propagation.
Microstructural heterogeneity creates local stress concentrations.
Microstructural heterogeneity creates spatially varying barriers to dislocation motion.
Quantifying local stress concentrations and dislocation barriers allows the model to capture elastic, yielding, and fracture responses.
The model may reduce computational-resource use by approximately 80%.
The model may predict Young’s modulus, yield strength, and fracture toughness within ±10% of experimental values.
Conventional atomistic or continuum full-field simulations require extensive computational resources for mechanical-property prediction.
Temperature can materially alter the mechanical response of refractory high-entropy alloys.
The approach may fail when temperature-dependent phenomena are not represented by the selected microstructural descriptors.
The approach may fail for HfNbTiVAl10 microstructures outside the model’s training domain because their dislocation behavior may differ unpredictably.
The actual prediction errors and efficiency gains may vary with testing conditions and sample variability.
